claims.text: Hexagonal boron nitride nanoplatelets are thermally stable and two-dimensional.
Adding h-BN nanoplatelets to CoCrFeNi will facilitate formation of a continuous h-BN-containing tribolayer during sliding.
The proposed tribolayer will remain effective from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C in air.
The h-BN nanoplatelets will remain structurally intact throughout the proposed temperature range.
A tribolayer containing h-BN nanoplatelets will create a low-shear sliding interface.
The low-shear interface will reduce friction.
Formation of a durable lubricious h-BN film will limit wear.
The h-BN-modified CoCrFeNi composite will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
The h-BN-modified CoCrFeNi composite will have better wear resistance than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the full temperature range.
The proposed comparison will use identical sliding, temperature, load, and atmospheric conditions for modified and unmodified samples.
High-temperature oxidation may compete with the proposed lubrication mechanism.
